content.comment_body: Hello, is it possible to connect two [company_name] [product_name] units wirelessly? I'm unable to run a network cable between them, so I'm wondering if a Wi-Fi point-to-point link could enable communication.
I'd recommend using a communication module with Modbus TCP and Wi-Fi support. Since [product_name] works with Modbus TCP, you can apply the same approach on both devices.

Wi-Fi, operating at 2.4 GHz and above, should provide adequate bandwidth. The [product_name] is sensitive in some cases, especially regarding specific connections. Keep in mind that Wi-Fi networks are shared with other devices, so using Modbus TCP might help manage data traffic more effectively, depending on your application. I have set up wireless point-to-point connections before, using industrial Bluetooth, although those solutions can be expensive.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are considering wireless methods to link two [product_name] units since installing network cables isn't feasible. They discuss the technical possibilities of Wi-Fi or industrial Bluetooth, potential issues due to shared networks, and the need for compatibility with existing protocols. Reliability and network sensitivity are noted concerns.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks a dependable and simple wireless solution for connecting two [product_name] units, aiming for compatibility with established protocols and functionality, without requiring network cabling.
